subject: Business
title: Viral Loops and Word of Mouth
description: A micro-lesson that makes Viral Loops and Word of Mouth usable.

hook.text: Hotmail added 'Get your free email at Hotmail' to every message. 12 million users in 18 months.

buildup.text: A viral loop means each new user naturally brings in more users as part of using the product.

discovery.text: The viral coefficient K measures this: if K is above 1, each user brings more than one new user.

twist.text: True virality is rare. Most 'viral' products grow through paid ads dressed up as organic buzz.

climax.text: Dropbox cracked it with referrals: give storage to get storage. Users became the sales team.

punchline.text: Make sharing part of using the product.

quiz.question: What does a viral coefficient (K) greater than 1 mean?
options: Each user brings in more than one new user on average
The product has over one million users

details.summary: Viral loops are built-in product mechanisms where existing users naturally bring in new users through sharing, inviting, or collaborating. When the viral coefficient exceeds one, meaning each user brings in more than one additional user, growth becomes exponential and self-sustaining without paid
details.whyItMatters: Viral loops create the most capital-efficient growth in business. Companies like WhatsApp, TikTok, and Zoom grew to billions of users with minimal marketing spend because the product itself was the growth engine through natural user-driven sharing.
takeaways: Viral loops make existing users the primary channel for bringing in new users
A viral coefficient above one means each user brings more than one new user
Viral products grow exponentially without proportional marketing investment

faq.question: What is a viral coefficient and how is it calculated?
faq.answer: The viral coefficient equals the number of invitations sent per user multiplied by the conversion rate of those invitations. If each user invites 5 people and 25 percent join, the coefficient is 1.25. Above 1.0 means exponential growth. Even 0.5 meaningfully reduces customer acquisition costs.

faq.question: Can virality be engineered into any product?
faq.answer: No. Truly viral products either require multiple users to function like messaging apps, generate shareable outputs like Canva designs, or create inherent social proof through visible usage. Artificial viral mechanics like forced sharing feel spammy and generate backlash rather than genuine growth.
